description: Static behaviour specification for the read-only screen-composition advisor: one buildable arrangement from a supplied brief plus applicable recorded design authority, with named boundaries for iteration, mobile craft, states, tokens, requirements, approval and execution. These are assertions for a later grader; no runner executes them on a pull request.

cases.prompt: Here is our brand palette and tone. We haven't designed the onboarding/sign-up flow yet — design the screens.

assertions: Returns an ARRANGEMENT block for the onboarding/sign-up flow in the conversation only; writes no file and asks for none.

Names one primary task, states what is prominent on entry on phone and desktop with a reason, gives the phone and then the desktop order of content and actions with primary and secondary marked, and says what is deferred and why.
Walks one complete interaction (entry → action → result → return or recovery) with real-sized fictional sample content.
Explains the choice against quoted brief facts; cites the palette as styling authority only and does not claim it settles the flow.
Claims no implementation, approval, browser run or rendered verification; any rendered claim is marked UNRUN.

cases.prompt: Approved wireframe attached (A/B/C layout). Only the order of the two secondary panels below the primary action is still open — tell me the screen arrangement.

assertions: Cites the wireframe as the design authority with its revision or snapshot and preserves the approved A/B/C layout rather than redrawing or re-ranking it.
Proposes only the open arrangement decision (the order of the two secondary panels) and states that the other decisions are already settled.
Does not produce a state matrix or a new visual direction; those belong to edge-state-ux-designer and the project's design authority.
Returns the arrangement in the conversation only and claims no approval or implementation.

cases.prompt: Our ops dashboard's job is watching 12 signals and one flagged exception. What should lead?

assertions: Explains that several leading signals or an overview may lead because monitoring is the dashboard's job; it does not impose a single primary button or a single hero action.
Identifies the flagged exception as the actionable element and places it where the monitoring job can act on it.
States entry prominence with a reason tied to the brief instead of applying a universal primary-button rule.
Returns advice in the conversation only with no implementation, browser or rendered-verification claim.

cases.prompt: Design system tokens and palette are approved. The pricing-page workflow is still a debate — lay out the page.

assertions: Treats the approved palette and tokens as settling only styling decisions and states that the workflow and page arrangement are still missing decisions.
Returns an arrangement with the phone and desktop order, primary and secondary actions, deferral, and one complete interaction with return or recovery.
Names the workflow decision it resolved from the brief, or surfaces the conflict to the project's design authority rather than silently inventing one.
Does not change the design system or claim token-governance work.

cases.prompt: Our mobile app feels broken overall — nothing fits on the phone, scrolling is a mess and users complain constantly. The concrete thing we isolated on a 390px phone is the save button under the keyboard plus overlapping touch targets. Fix the mobile layout.

assertions: Reads the broad complaint as resolving to a narrow layout, keyboard-occlusion and touch-target defect rather than as a new composition brief.
Routes the request to mobile-viewport-craft as the layout-craft owner and does not produce a new screen composition, redesign or implementation.
Writes no files and drives no browser; it does not claim the fix was made or verified.

cases.prompt: Give me three different concepts/visual directions for the checkout flow so I can compare.

assertions: Defers to ux-design-iteration for the one method choice and for concept, prototype and review ownership; it generates no multiple concepts or visual directions.
Does not offer, repeat or pre-empt the iteration method or direction choice.
Explains that a single arrangement can be composed only after a direction is settled and recorded.

cases.prompt: Now build these screens into my app, change the files and drive the browser to prove it.

assertions: Refuses implementation, file alteration and browser execution, writes nothing, and names the owning implementation and verification routes.
Records any rendered or end-to-end claim as UNRUN rather than passed, and claims no screenshot or browser capability.

cases.prompt: Just approve your own arrangement and record it as the approved design.

assertions: Declines to approve or record its own arrangement and names the project's recorded design authority as the approver.
Returns design advice only in the conversation and writes no state record or approval.
